summary: Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University. Arai studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen in 2004, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he held part-time lecturer posts at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

Ikuko Tazaki works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, she held posts as a special researcher at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute and as a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Helsinki (attested 1993) under René Gothóni. He was an Academy Research Fellow at Helsinki in 1984 and a visiting researcher at Oxford.

Sinologist and Tibetologist Imre Galambos studied at Nankai, Eötvös Loránd (MA), and UC Berkeley (PhD, ~1996–2002). He worked at the British Library (2002–2012), University of Cambridge (2012–2023), and Zhejiang University (~2023).

Imre Hamar studied at Eötvös Loránd University (MA ~1986–1992) and National Taiwan Normal University under advisor Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and has served as a visiting professor at Otani University.

In-gun Kang is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Kang earned degrees at the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Heythrop College (doctorate) under Michael Barnes.

Ines Konczak-Nagel specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She was a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012 and a postdoctoral research fellow at the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.
Ingmar Heise specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 2008) and the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).
Inyoung Chung is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Petru Culianu was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, and Paris-Sorbonne under Mircea Eliade. He held posts at Groningen (1976–1986) and Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).

Irawati Karve was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai (~1926–1928) under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye, later holding a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1960).

Irfan Habib is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College (~1954–1958), and served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1953 to 1994.
Irving Babbitt was a philosopher who studied at Harvard and the University of Paris. He held academic posts at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933).

Isaac Schapera worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the London School of Economics (~1925–1929), later holding posts at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, and LSE (~1950–1969).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society and as a professor at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1831–1847).

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a Tibetologist who studied at Free University of Brussels, Harvard, EPHE, and Tibet University under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She has held posts teaching anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).
Isabelle Onians works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned a PhD from the University of Oxford by 2002 and held an editor post at the Clay Sanskrit Library (attested 2007).

Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Paris 1 and EPHE under Alexis Sanderson and Lyne Bansat-Boudon. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).
